title: Completion Walkthrough, Punch Items and Job Close-Out — Installation Jobs
content:
**Crew lead handbook — completing and closing an Installation Jobs record**

## Completion

At the end of the last crew day the crew lead and the customer walk every opening, record any item still to finish or correct as a punch item, and the customer signs the completion certificate; the job is completed on the date of that signature.

Completion starts warranty coverage for the contract, closes the factory order, starts the contract's final balance clock and is the document the financing lender needs to fund.

## Punch items

Punch items are resolved within the method's response window counted in business days from the day after completion; a punch item never delays completion. A punch item is recorded by its kind — caulk touch-up, missing screen, hardware adjustment, trim damage, glass scratch or cleanup — with the openings it affects, and is resolved by a record naming that item.

## Closing

A job is closed only when every punch item logged on it has been resolved. A permitted job also waits for its final inspection to pass before it closes.

The open punch items of a job are the punch items logged on that job that no resolution record names, counted over the job's lifetime up to the moment of handling; the test is made on the job's own system records.

## Close-out table

| Every punch item logged on the job resolved | Job permitted | Final inspection passed | Job may close |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | No | — | Yes |
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Yes | Yes | No | No |
| No | either | either | No |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A job is signed off on a Monday with two punch items open. It is completed that Monday; the two items do not delay completion.
- Of three punch items logged on a job, two have been resolved. The job is not closed while the third remains open.
